articles.title: Welcome to SJAA
articles.summary: This article introduces Steven Nelson as SJAA's new Director2 and QuickStart Program Leader. Nelson, an astronomy major from UC Berkeley and former STEM teacher, brings extensive professional and amateur telescope experience, including work on the Hubble's Faint Object Spectrograph and at major observatories like Lick and Mauna Kea. He expresses enthusiasm for rejoining SJAA's public education mission, having previously served on its Board around the turn of the century.

articles.title: In Memoriam Don Machholz
articles.summary: This article is an 'In Memoriam' tribute to Don Machholz (1952-2022), a renowned comet hunter, SJAA member, and co-inventor of the Messier Marathon, who passed away unexpectedly from COVID-19 at age 69. It highlights his significant contributions to the astronomy community, including his podcast 'Looking Up With Don,' articles for EarthSky, and his regular 'Comet Comments' in the SJAA Ephemeris. Friends and colleagues fondly remember him for his kindness, legendary status, and his dedication to public astronomy education.

articles.title: Origin of the Constellations
articles.summary: This article explores the origins of constellations, tracing many common names back to ancient Middle Eastern, Greek, and Roman cultures, while also acknowledging similar star-grouping traditions worldwide. It details the addition of modern constellations by astronomers from the 1500s-1700s and the International Astronomical Union's 1930 standardization of 88 constellations. The piece also shares a Native American Navajo folktale explaining the creation of stars and the incomplete nature of some star patterns, emphasizing the role of cultural narratives in understanding the night sky.

articles.title: Comet Headed Our Way
articles.summary: Comet C/2022 E3 ZTF, discovered on March 2, 2022, is anticipated to be a significant topic in the astronomy community as it approaches its closest points to the Sun (January 13, 2023) and Earth (February 2, 2023). Predicted to reach a peak magnitude of 5.5, it may be visible to the naked eye and easily with binoculars, positioned high in the northern sky. The author has already observed and showcased the comet at public star parties, expecting media attention as the end of 2022 approaches.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: The SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery features recent astrophotography submissions from club members, showcasing deep-sky objects like WR134, NGC 6914, Caldwell 100, and M 27. Each entry provides comprehensive details including the imaging dates, locations, and the specific telescopes, cameras, mounts, and software utilized by the astrophotographers.

articles.title: Using Cepheids As Distance Measures
articles.summary: This article outlines a method for measuring stellar distances using Cepheid variable stars, specifically Delta Cephei. Observers are instructed to record Delta Cephei's brightness variations over time to determine its period, which is then used to find its absolute magnitude. Finally, the absolute and apparent magnitudes are applied in the distance modulus formula to calculate the star's distance from Earth.

articles.title: Hubble Views a Galactic Marvel
articles.summary: The article highlights a new Hubble Space Telescope image of NGC 1156, a dwarf irregular galaxy with a unique shape that blends features of both spiral and elliptical galaxies, showcasing intense star formation. Located 25 million light-years away in Aries, it is classified as an isolated galaxy. This observation is part of a 'gap-filling' program designed to capture detailed images of nearby galaxies not previously studied sufficiently by Hubble.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: NASA's Mars Sample Return Program has finalized its conceptual design phase, outlining a revised architecture to bring Martian samples to Earth by 2033. The updated plan leverages the Perseverance rover's longevity and adds two Ingenuity-like helicopters for sample retrieval, eliminating the need for a separate Sample Fetch Rover. This international collaboration with ESA aims to reduce mission complexity and increase success probability.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board of Directors has been actively reconvening in-person activities following the lifting of mask mandates and held several meetings in June, July, and August 2022. Key decisions included changing the fiscal year, implementing sign-in sheets for events, approving a Code of Conduct for leadership, and establishing a Protection of Minors Policy. Additionally, the board approved funds for solar program equipment and discussed ongoing operational concerns, bylaw maintenance, and asset inventory for compliance reporting.

articles.title: SJAA Programs and Resources
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a diverse range of programs and resources designed to support and educate both novice and experienced astronomy enthusiasts. These include a library, telescope repair sessions, and monthly observing events for solar and night sky viewing. SJAA also provides beginner guidance programs, an equipment loaner program, specialized astro-imaging groups and workshops, and hosts educational star parties for schools and the community.
